items.title: The literal full precision, including its residual identity block

source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS mathematical restatement.

items.statement: Within the standing range kappa>=4 and 3<=n<=d, put k=floor(d/n). For every tuple of k real orthogonal n by n matrices, define the d by d precision as diag(A_O1,...,A_Ok,I_(d-kn)), where A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T).
assumptions: d and n are natural dimensions; kappa is a real number.
n>=3, n<=d and kappa>=4 are the source standing range.
O is a tuple indexed by Fin(d/n), with each matrix in the full real orthogonal group on Fin n.
The literal algebraic definition extends to every natural d,n and real kappa; spectral and minimizer theorems retain the source range.

obligations.label: The literal full precision, including its residual identity block

bindings.boundary: Only determinant-family regularity and the quadratic minimum in Lemma3.4/B.8. Gaussian normalization, Haar posterior laws, oracle indistinguishability, test separation and both main complexity lower bounds remain open.

assumption_deltas.lean: The theorem retains n>=3,n<=d,kappa>=4; Fin(d/n) blocks and Fin(d%n) residual, with contiguous coordinate equivalence.
assumption_deltas.reason: Euclidean division identifies d%n with d-k*n. Real Hermitianity and universal dot-product bounds express source symmetry and Loewner bounds; no Pi norm or entrywise matrix order is used.

assumption_deltas.source: The source introduces the formula in its standing range.
assumption_deltas.lean: The same literal block expression is defined for all natural d,n and real kappa.
assumption_deltas.reason: This is an algebraic carrier extension with no invented off-source fallback. It asserts no spectral or minimizer conclusion outside the standing range.

items.title: Sum the actual single-block estimates in the original coordinates

source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS mathematical restatement.

items.statement: For n>=3,n<=d,kappa>=4 and every tuple of floor(d/n) real orthogonal n by n matrices, the literal d-dimensional precision A is symmetric and every x in R^d satisfies x^T x<=x^T A x<=kappa x^T x. Hence A belongs to the source admissible precision class.
assumptions: d and n are natural dimensions; kappa is a real number.
n>=3, n<=d and kappa>=4 are the source standing range.
O is a tuple indexed by Fin(d/n), with each matrix in the full real orthogonal group on Fin n.

formulae.label: Lemma3.4/B.8
formulae.tex: A=A^\top,\qquad \|x\|_2^2\le x^\top A x\le\kappa\|x\|_2^2\quad(\forall x\in\mathbb R^d)

items.title: The quadratic potential has its unique minimum at zero

source.attribution: Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki, On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling. ASTIS mathematical restatement.

items.statement: Under the same n>=3,n<=d,kappa>=4 and orthogonal tuple assumptions, the actual potential f_A(x)=(1/2)x^T A x has f_A(0)=0, is nonnegative for every x, and equals zero if and only if x=0. Thus its unique minimizer is0 and its minimum value is0.
assumptions: d and n are natural dimensions; kappa is a real number.
n>=3, n<=d and kappa>=4 are the source standing range.
O is a tuple indexed by Fin(d/n), with each matrix in the full real orthogonal group on Fin n.

assumption_deltas.source: Unique minimizer0 and minimum value0; strict positivity for nonzero x.
assumption_deltas.lean: Value0 at0, nonnegativity at every x, and zero value iff x=0.
assumption_deltas.reason: Over the reals, nonnegativity and the exact zero set imply positivity off0 and the same unique minimum. The potential is the actual displayed quadratic form, not an unspecified objective.
